name: Propylene glycol

name_warning.note: The upstream taxonomy calls E490 propylene glycol. FSSAI's own compendium states that propylene glycol is INS 1520, and does not list 490. Until that is resolved, nothing is claimed about what this number denotes.

what_it_is: Open Food Facts lists this number as propylene glycol, but FSSAI assigns propylene glycol to INS 1520. We could not confirm what INS 490 means in Indian rules.
why_its_added: Not stated here, because the substance behind this number is not confirmed.

india.note: Maximum level depends on the food. Examples below.

usa.note: Generally Recognised As Safe (GRAS) for direct addition to food (21 CFR 184.1666)

means: No single-serving limit has been found for this substance. That is not the same as there being no risk from one large serving - it means nobody has published a number.

people_reports.rule: Reports are shown as reports. We count them. We never turn them into a health claim, and we never let them change the sourced facts above.
